title: Signal Imprinter
pages: Craft the Signal Imprinter with iron, copper, one antimony ingot (forge:ingots/antimony), a Stator Coil, one Laminated Shell from the Armor Delaminator and one Transformer Core. Press two more Laminated Shells into the core (160 ticks, 10 FE/t); its compressed insulated laminae carry the alternating field for the signal head. Feed shells to the Pressure Press from above, supply FE, and extract the core below. Its Signal Matrix unlocks the Resonant Cultivator before the Electrolyzer.

Place a redstone block below the controller and a lightning rod above it. Put iron blocks to the north and south, copper blocks to the east and west, and redstone lamps at all four horizontal corners. The ten surrounding parts make a signal lattice; any missing lamp or bus breaks formation. Right-click the formed controller with a full recipe batch; an incomplete structure or unlisted input is refused. One batch loads into the stock buffer, then completes after 40 ticks; collect the product with an empty hand or through the bottom face.

Twenty-one exclusive signal imprinting recipes make repeaters, comparators, rails, sensors, dispensers and other useful redstone components from bulk feedstock. The batch costs are deliberately greater than ordinary crafting; this is a compact one-input conversion route. Two Laminated Shells also fuse into a Signal Matrix for future progression.

This controller needs no FE or fluids; it can be hand-fed or automated (see the automation page). By hand, load one full batch, wait 40 ticks, then collect buffered output with an empty hand. JEI lists each input batch and output under Signal Imprinting; the Signal Imprinter is its catalyst. Datapacks may add signal_imprinting recipes; ties use resource ID order.

Automation: the controller also keeps a one-stack stock buffer and a one-stack product buffer. Hoppers, droppers and sided item pipes insert from the top and the four sides; only items that match a loaded signal imprinting recipe are accepted, and simulated inserts never change the buffer. While the structure is formed and owned, it runs one batch every 40 ticks (2 seconds) without power, using the same recipe priority as hand use (lowest resource ID first). Products wait in the buffer and are pulled from the bottom face, e.g. by a hopper under a Stock Hatch that replaces the base part. If the structure breaks, work pauses and progress resets; if the product buffer is full or holds a different item, work waits. Sneak-use with an empty hand on a face to cycle it between In, Out and Off; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered products. Buffers, progress and face settings are saved with the chunk, and breaking the controller drops both buffers.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer.
